name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,829

clue.text: Machine that supplies more tightly packed boxes is quiet

indicators.note: To box something is to shut it in a box, so the letters before it close round the letters after it.

blocks.note: packed more tightly is denser
the word goes in as written
p = piano, the sheet-music mark for playing quietly

explanation.surface: A vending machine crammed so full of boxes that it has stopped making any noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like the machine's stock and is in fact the verb that wraps one word round another. The p arriving inside comes from music, where piano means quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser is the machine you take a paper cup, a squirt of soap or a chocolate bar from, one helping at a time.

clue.text: Detectives eating lots turned up full of beans

indicators.note: What is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one set of letters sits within the other.
In a down entry 'up' sends the letters back towards the top of the grid, so the whole assembly reads the other way round.

blocks.note: the CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, its plain-clothes detectives, here climbing the grid
lots of something is many, also on its way up

explanation.surface: Plain-clothes officers put away a huge meal and come away bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The meal reads as the detectives' dinner, but 'full of beans' is the definition. Assembled downwards the letters spell CIMANYD, and only the climb back up makes a word of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of beans is bouncing with energy, which is what calling a person dynamic claims for them.

clue.text: Melanesian for one day, I lie about

blocks.note: a solo is for one performer alone
Mon is the diary's short form of Monday
the letter as written
a slander is a lie told about somebody

explanation.surface: A diary entry: for one day the writer turns Melanesian and lies about doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has someone lazing around, but a lie told about a person is a slander, and that is the work 'lie about' is really doing. Mon is the diary's Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solomon Islands sit in Melanesia, so anyone from them is a Melanesian.

clue.text: Fictitious details troubled bride more, close to ceremony

indicators.note: Something troubled has been shaken out of its settled state, and letters called troubled will not stay in the order given.
'Close to' asks for the very end of the word that follows, the letter it closes with.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters
the closing letter of ceremonY

explanation.surface: As the ceremony nears, something upsets the bride even more than before.
explanation.walkthrough: To embroider a tale is to sew extra bits onto it, which is how needlework came to mean lying. The wedding words keep you thinking about actual thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Embroidery is the invented trimming added to a story — the details that were never true.

clue.text: Slope, white and cordial in fine weather

indicators.note: 'In' puts what comes before it inside what comes after, so the drink goes within the weather.

blocks.note: fine weather is sun
a kir is white wine with a measure of blackcurrant cordial stirred into it

explanation.surface: A white hillside under a warm sun, and a welcome as friendly as the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' reads as the friendly welcome and is a bottle of blackcurrant syrup: white wine plus that syrup is a kir, the French aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is the prepared descent you come down a mountain on, which is a slope.

clue.text: Large bottle tramp wrapped with much paper

indicators.note: To be wrapped with something is to have it closed round you, so the paper goes outside and the man inside.

blocks.note: a ream is 500 sheets, a lot of paper
a hobo is a tramp

explanation.surface: A tramp keeps the cold out under a thick bundle of newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant champagne bottles are named after biblical kings — a rehoboam is six ordinary bottles in one, and Rehoboam was Solomon's son.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam holds six standard bottles of champagne, so it answers plainly to 'large bottle'.

clue.text: Bishop must return to queen's boudoir

blocks.note: b = bishop in chess notation
to owe is to be under obligation to return what you have had
r = Regina, Latin for queen, as on royal cyphers

explanation.surface: A chess bishop is sent back to the queen's private room.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess supplies the b and royal cyphers the r. Between them, 'must return' is not a move on the board but the verb owe.
explanation.definitionFit: In older poetry a bower is a lady's private chamber, the room a boudoir names.

clue.text: How might kids get to school with Tesla on the blink?

blocks.clueFragment: How might kids get to school
blocks.note: the school bus is how they get there
t = tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: With the family's Tesla broken down, how are the children supposed to reach school?
explanation.walkthrough: Nikola Tesla has a unit named after him, the tesla, whose symbol is T — which is why the electric car in the surface is a decoy. The question mark covers the roundabout way the bus is named.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing on the blink has stopped working, which is what bust says of it.

clue.text: If quartet chosen to play on the radio, piece after the news?

indicators.note: What reaches you on the radio arrives as sound alone, so the letters follow how the words are said rather than how they are spelt.

blocks.note: 'if' introduces a whether-or-not, and whether is said exactly like the other spelling
a quartet is four, and performers chosen to play a part are cast

explanation.surface: A quartet has been picked to perform on air, slotted in once the news bulletin ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are pure sound, and 'cast' is the theatre's word for who has been chosen to play. 'Piece' reads as a piece of music; it means the item in a running order.
explanation.definitionFit: On radio and television the forecast is the item that follows the news, so it is defined here by its place in the schedule.

clue.text: Nuts near kid quickly piled up

indicators.note: Somebody nuts is not in their right order, and letters called nuts come out of theirs.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: Nuts have been heaped up in a hurry beside a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' opens the clue looking like the snack on the table and is the instruction to disorder what follows it. Money is what gets raked in — by casinos, hit shows and lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake something in is to gather it into heaps at speed, the way a croupier sweeps chips off a table.

clue.text: Love playing football?

blocks.note: read as being keen on the game, and meant as a score of nothing, which is what love counts in tennis
the sport is the whole point: a football score of nothing is never read out as love

explanation.surface: A question about whether somebody enjoys a game of football.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is tennis's word for a score of nothing; football announces the same score with a different word, and the question mark carries you between the two sports.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is how nothing is read out in a football score — Sunderland two, Newcastle nil — where tennis would say love.

clue.text: Smartie from vividly coloured box kid's opening

indicators.note: A word's opening is the letter it starts with, and nothing else of it is wanted.

blocks.note: vividly coloured is bright
to spar is to box, trading practice punches
the opening letter of kid

explanation.surface: A sweet rolls out of the garish tube a child has just opened.
explanation.walkthrough: The sweets are the decoy: a smartie is also a person who thinks fast. 'Box' is the verb, sparring rather than packaging, and the apostrophe-s on kid hides a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright spark is someone quick and clever, said admiringly or sarcastically, which is exactly what a smartie is.

clue.text: Silly jargon posh doctor fed to mother and father of 8?

indicators.note: Whatever is fed to someone goes inside them, so those letters are swallowed by the words that follow.

blocks.note: mum = mother
BoJo is the tabloids' name for Boris Johnson, British prime minister from 2019 to 2022 and reportedly a father of eight
u = upper class, from the U and non-U of class-marked English
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A posh doctor talks nonsense at a mother and at the father of eight children.
explanation.walkthrough: That 8 looks like a cross-reference to another clue and is a tally of children: the 'father of 8' is Boris Johnson, BoJo in every headline of his premiership.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo-jumbo is talk dressed up to sound expert while meaning nothing, which is silly jargon.

clue.text: Chas Hodges hiding in Boots?

indicators.note: Something hiding is in full view but unremarked, so the letters sit unbroken inside the words as written.

blocks.note: chaS HODges — Chas Hodges was the Chas of Chas & Dave, the cockney piano-and-bass duo of 'Snooker Loopy'

explanation.surface: Chas Hodges is spotted lurking in a branch of Boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is Britain's high-street chemist, and the capital letter is what makes footwear look like a shop you could hide in.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe is a verb as well as a thing — blacksmiths shoe horses — and its past participle covers anybody walking about in footwear.

clue.text: Finest street full of building society employees after evacuation

indicators.note: A street full of something has it inside, so those letters go within the letters of the street.
An evacuated building is emptied of everyone in it and only the shell is left, which for a word means its two end letters.

blocks.note: st = street, as written on an address
a building society is a British mutual that lends people the money for their houses
EmployeeS emptied out keeps only the letters at its two ends

explanation.surface: The staff of a building society stand in the street after the alarm went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building society' is one phrase, not a building and a society: in Britain it is a mutual lender like Nationwide. Evacuation empties a word as thoroughly as it empties an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine can mean thin — a fine thread, fine hair — so the finest of several is the most slender.

clue.text: Miraculous wedding venue daughter saw on the inside, Celine Dion's home once

indicators.note: What is on the inside of a word is its middle letter, the one furthest from either end.

blocks.note: at the wedding in Cana in Galilee the water was turned into wine
d = daughter, as in a family tree
the middle letter of sAw

explanation.surface: A daughter got a look inside the venue where the famous wedding miracle happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Cana earns its place in crosswords by being four useful letters and the site of the first miracle. Celine Dion is Québécoise, raised near Montreal long before her Las Vegas residency.
explanation.definitionFit: Celine Dion grew up in Charlemagne, Quebec, so Canada is the country she called home before the Las Vegas years.

clue.text: 100 litres in a round cooking pot

indicators.note: Cooking stirs ingredients until none of them is where it was put, and letters can be stirred the same way.

blocks.note: c = 100 in Roman numerals
l = litre, the unit's symbol
the word joins the mixture as written
anagram fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: A hundred litres of something go into a big round cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking pot' looks like one phrase, and splitting it is the whole difficulty: the cooking is the instruction and 'pot' alone defines. Roman numerals give the c and the litre its l.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is the big pot hung over a fire, so pot is the plain word for what it is.

clue.text: Flooded land upset tennis organisers and opponents

indicators.note: Something upset has been tipped over, and in a down entry that sends its letters back up towards the top.

blocks.note: the LTA, the Lawn Tennis Association, runs the game in Britain, and here those letters climb the grid
the antis are the people against whatever is proposed

explanation.surface: A flood wrecks the courts, annoying the tennis authorities and the campaigners against them alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as everybody's annoyance and is the instruction to turn three letters round. Plato tells the story of Atlantis being swallowed by the sea in a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island that sank beneath the ocean, which leaves it land under water.

clue.text: Level of interest shown by Spooner's hare at the dog track?

indicators.note: Spooner's version of a two-word phrase swaps the sounds the two words begin with.

blocks.note: the hare at a greyhound track is the mechanical lure the dogs chase, the bait of the race; trade the opening sounds of those two words

explanation.surface: Greyhounds tear round the track after the mechanical hare.
explanation.walkthrough: Greyhound racing runs a dummy hare on a rail ahead of the dogs, which is the 'bait'. 'Level of interest' reads as how keen somebody is, and means a percentage.
explanation.definitionFit: The base rate is the interest rate the Bank of England sets, the level every other lender works from.

clue.text: Little sibling that's revolting teenager initially took along

indicators.note: 'Initially' asks for the letter a word starts with and nothing more of it.

blocks.note: a sibling is a brother, and the little version of the word is bro
ugh is the noise you make at something revolting
the initial letter of teenager

explanation.surface: A teenager drags a disgusting younger sibling along too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's revolting' describes nobody: it is the noise of disgust itself, ugh. The three pieces then stack in the order the clue hands them over, which charades rarely do.
explanation.definitionFit: If you brought something, you took it along with you — brought is simply the past tense of bring.

clue.text: Only half studying insects book, put Six Feet down?

indicators.note: 'Only half' keeps one half of the word and throws the other half away.

blocks.note: studying insects is entomology, ten letters, of which half is ENTOM
b = book

explanation.surface: Someone skimming an insect textbook puts down their box set of Six Feet Under.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics flag Six Feet Under, the drama set in a family funeral home, so putting six feet down is burying. Entomology is long enough that half of it is still five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to shut a body away in a tomb — put it six feet down, as the gravediggers' measure has it.

clue.text: Too many drinks, taking leak in bar that's spinning

indicators.note: 'In' puts what comes before it inside what comes after, rather than beside it.
Something spinning comes round to face the other way, so those letters arrive back to front.

blocks.note: a pub is a bar, spun round to read BUP
to ooze is to leak slowly

explanation.surface: After one drink too many the room is spinning and someone slips off to the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leak' is the drinker's trip to the gents on the surface and the verb ooze in the wordplay. The bar spins because the letters of pub have to arrive backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze-up is a session of heavy drinking, which is what too many drinks adds up to.

clue.text: Wanting part from autopsy, choose nut

indicators.note: To want part of something is to want a piece taken out of it, and the piece here is a run of letters lifted whole.

blocks.note: autoPSY, CHOose — the letters run straight across the comma

explanation.surface: Offered a part from the post-mortem, somebody picks the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies unbroken across the comma, which is where hidden words like to sit. 'Nut' is the definition in its lunatic sense, not the surface's piece of anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho is a dangerously unhinged person, and nut is the everyday slang for one.

clue.text: Virtuous releasing maiden from one's trap

indicators.note: Releasing something lets it go, so that letter leaves the word it was being held in.

blocks.note: a virtuous person is moral
m = maiden, cricket's over with no runs off it, and the letter set free here

explanation.surface: A virtuous hero lets a maiden out of somebody's snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is slang for the mouth, so the definition is about speech and not about rescue. Cricket's scoreless over supplies the m that has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken — coming out of one's trap, trap being the rude word for the mouth.

clue.text: Invest wrongly, easily receive nothing

indicators.note: Do a thing wrongly and it comes out other than it should, which for letters means out of their proper order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters
to get something is to receive it
nothing is written as a nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: Put your money in the wrong place and you will easily end up with nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' is doing military service here: to invest a town is to surround it with an army. The whole financial surface is built out of the other meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In its military sense, to invest a town or castle is to ring it with troops and besiege it.

clue.text: Primitive accommodation English hoover up

indicators.note: In a down entry 'up' takes the letters back towards the top of the grid, so they read the other way round.

blocks.note: a vac is a vacuum cleaner — Hoover is the brand Britain uses as the word — and it goes up the grid
e = English

explanation.surface: An English vacuum cleaner is sucking up the last of the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoover up' reads as one phrase, the vacuuming, and is two separate instructions: the vac, and the climb that turns it round. E for English then lands at the bottom of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave is the shelter people lived in before they built anything, which makes it accommodation of the most primitive kind.

clue.text: Crook got lad price for Higgs boson

indicators.note: Something crook is bent out of true, and letters bent out of true come out in another order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A shady dealer quotes a young man a price for the Higgs boson.
explanation.walkthrough: The nickname comes from a popular-science book: Leon Lederman wanted a ruder title and his publisher printed 'The God Particle' instead. 'Crook' opens the clue looking like the villain of the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Higgs boson is the particle everyone outside physics knows as the God particle, after the book that coined the phrase.

clue.text: Do away with unlimited tariffs

indicators.note: Something unlimited has no limits, so the word loses the letters at both its ends.

blocks.note: tariffs are taxes, and with its limits gone the word keeps only its middle

explanation.surface: A government promises to scrap tariffs that have no ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' is the standard instruction for a word with both end letters taken off. The surface stays a piece of trade policy from first word to last.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to abolish it at a stroke — a job, a service, a programme — which is doing away with it.

clue.text: Mobile service provider without ties, according to Danny Dyer?

indicators.note: Naming whose voice to hear asks for the word as that speaker says it, so sound counts and spelling does not.

blocks.note: free = without ties, and in the London accent Danny Dyer speaks in, the answer comes out as 'free'

explanation.surface: Danny Dyer explains which network will let you go contract-free.
explanation.walkthrough: Danny Dyer is an English actor famous for a broad cockney accent, and cockney turns the th of this word into an f. The definition is a brand name rather than a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is one of Britain's mobile phone networks, which makes it a mobile service provider.

clue.text: Trousers spinner gives close fielder

blocks.note: shorts are trousers cut off above the knee
a top is the toy you set spinning

explanation.surface: A spin bowler's trousers somehow produce a fielder standing close to the bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word points at cricket and the answer belongs to baseball. 'Spinner' is the child's toy, not the bowler turning his arm over.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop guards the infield gap between second and third base, the closest-in fielding position baseball has.
